evidence_used: Object is a rigid plastic component storage box with flat, smooth, parallel sidewalls suitable for gecko adhesive pads.
Surface appears clean and nonporous, matching optimal dry-adhesion conditions.
calculation_summary: F_normal = F_pre-load + (Estimated Weight / Maximum Adhesion Efficiency Factor). Given high gecko adhesion on smooth flat plastic, a minimal pre-load normal force of 0.5 N is sufficient to establish initial contact and engage the dry adhesive pads.
assumptions_and_uncertainty: Exact object mass and center of mass are visually estimated due to lack of authoritative sensor measurements.
Sidewalls are assumed sufficiently flat and accessible for full pad engagement.
reasoning_trace: The target object is a clear plastic organizer box with smooth, flat sides, presenting an ideal substrate for gecko-inspired dry adhesives. Because dry adhesives achieve high directional holding performance on smooth, clean, nonporous surfaces with minimal clamping force, only a low normal preload force (0.5 N) is necessary to seat the pads and allow the adhesion to support the object against gravity.
